---
title: "Forest"
subtitle: "Plot data, then the covariates and training data behind each map, then the maps compared with each other."
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("_setup.R")
xl <- function(s) read_excel(xlsx, sheet = s)
studies <- xl("Studies"); ground <- xl("Ground_data"); links <- xl("Study_ground"); cov <- xl("Covariates")
forest_studies <- c("S_SOTHE_FOREST_2022", "S_SCANFI_V1", "S_BETTS_2024", "S_QIN_2025", "S_MATASCI_2018", "S_LAMPING_2025")
forest_ground <- c("G_NFI", "G_NFI_PHOTO", "G_QUEBEC", "G_CLI", "G_BC_INVENTORY", "G_ENFOR", "G_ABOVE", "G_VSN", "G_CASFRI")
```

::: {.domain-forest}

## 1. Plot data {#plots}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Placeholder.** No forest plot data is ingested yet, so there is nothing to compare at plot locations. When plots arrive, this section will compare plot-level biomass or carbon with each map at the plot's pixel, at the map's native grid, following the soil-profile method on the [Soils page](soils.qmd#profiles-vs-maps).
:::

The sources below are catalogued. Open downloads are the quickest route to a first plot comparison.

```{r}
used_by <- links |> left_join(studies |> select(study_id, study_name), by = "study_id") |>
  group_by(ground_id) |> summarise(used_by = paste0(study_name, " (", study_role, ")", collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")
ground |> filter(ground_id %in% forest_ground) |>
  left_join(used_by, by = "ground_id") |>
  arrange(match(ground_id, forest_ground)) |>
  transmute(Resource = resource_name, Measures = carbon_pool_or_measurement, Coverage = geographic_coverage,
            `Plot support` = coalesce(observation_support, "–"),
            Access = access_route, `Used by` = coalesce(used_by, "–")) |>
  kable()
```

## 2. Covariates and training data {#covariates}

Each forest map comes from a model trained on a different kind of reference data, at a different scale. The training data matter as much as the covariates when maps disagree.

```{r}
tr <- links |> left_join(ground |> select(ground_id, resource_name), by = "ground_id") |>
  group_by(study_id) |> summarise(training = paste0(resource_name, " (", study_role, ")", collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")
studies |> filter(study_id %in% forest_studies) |>
  left_join(tr, by = "study_id") |>
  left_join(cov |> group_by(study_id) |> summarise(n_cov = n(), .groups = "drop"), by = "study_id") |>
  arrange(match(study_id, forest_studies)) |>
  transmute(Study = study_name, Target = carbon_pool_or_target, Geography = analysis_geography,
            `Training / reference data` = coalesce(training, "–"),
            `Plot support` = coalesce(ground_observation_support, "–"),
            `Output grid (m)` = ifelse(is.na(output_grid_m), "–", fmt_n(output_grid_m)),
            `Covariate entries` = coalesce(as.character(n_cov), "0"),
            `Predictive evidence` = coalesce(predictive_evidence, "–")) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: chart-forest-scale
#| fig-height: 3.2
sc <- cov |> filter(study_id %in% forest_studies) |>
  mutate(native = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(native_grid_m)), output = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(output_grid_m))) |>
  left_join(studies |> select(study_id, study_name), by = "study_id")
out_df <- sc |> group_by(study_name) |> summarise(output = suppressWarnings(max(output, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") |> filter(is.finite(output))
ggplot(sc |> filter(!is.na(native)), aes(native, study_name)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = study_name), colour = pal$s1, alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 2.4) +
  geom_point(colour = pal$s1, size = 2.2) +
  geom_point(data = out_df, aes(output, study_name), shape = 23, size = 3.4, fill = pal$ink, colour = "white") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(10, 25, 30, 100, 250, 1000), labels = c("10 m", "25 m", "30 m", "100 m", "250 m", "1 km")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Native covariate grids (blue) versus output grid (diamond)",
       subtitle = "A 400 m² inventory plot is about one 20 × 20 m footprint: finer than every output grid here")
```

```{r}
#| label: chart-forest-families
#| fig-height: 3
grp <- c(`Temporal optical` = "Optical time series", Optical = "Optical reflectance", Reflectance = "Optical reflectance",
         `Sentinel-2` = "Optical reflectance", `Remote sensing` = "Optical reflectance", Radar = "Radar", Backscattering = "Radar",
         `Sentinel-1` = "Radar", Structure = "Canopy structure", Climate = "Climate & temperature", Temperature = "Climate & temperature",
         Terrain = "Terrain", Environment = "Land cover & ecology")
fam <- cov |> filter(study_id %in% forest_studies) |> mutate(group = coalesce(grp[family], family)) |>
  count(study_id, group, evidence_level) |> left_join(studies |> select(study_id, study_name), by = "study_id")
ggplot(fam, aes(group, study_name, fill = evidence_level)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), colour = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Model input` = pal$s1, `Retained/ranked family` = pal$seq[6], `Reported importance` = pal$seq[7]), name = "Evidence") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Covariate entries by family and evidence level") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

## 3. Maps compared with each other {#maps}

**The McMaster/WWF comparison comes first** because it is the most cited Canadian forest carbon map. Statistics and maps both come from 30,000 area-uniform random points, read on each pair's coarser native grid; points where both products are zero (non-forest in both) are left out.

### McMaster/WWF forest carbon vs SCANFI aboveground carbon {#mcmaster-scanfi}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**The pools differ, so read the difference carefully.** McMaster/WWF (Sothe et al. 2022) maps aboveground, belowground and dead plant carbon in kg C/m². SCANFI v1.2 maps aboveground biomass; it is converted to carbon here as biomass × 0.5 (carbon fraction) × 0.1 (t/ha to kg/m²). McMaster minus SCANFI carbon therefore mixes belowground and dead carbon with genuine disagreement about aboveground carbon, and cannot be read as either alone. McMaster inputs mostly represent 2015–2019; SCANFI is 2020. SCANFI (30 m) is averaged to the McMaster ≈250 m grid.
:::

```{r}
mcm <- read_pair_samples("mcm_forest")
if (!is.null(mcm)) mcm <- mcm |> filter(a > 0 | b > 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: chart-mcm-maps
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.3
#| fig-cap: !expr hex_caption(100000, 5)
if (!is.null(mcm)) hex_trio(mcm, "kg C/m²", "McMaster/WWF (above + below + dead)", "SCANFI aboveground × 0.5")
```

```{r}
#| label: chart-mcm
#| fig-height: 4.2
if (!is.null(mcm)) {
  hex_pair(mcm, "kg C/m²", "McMaster/WWF", "SCANFI carbon", bins = 50) | ecozone_bias(mcm, "kg C/m²", "McMaster/WWF", "SCANFI carbon")
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(mcm)) {
  mcm |> group_by(id) |> agree_stats() |> mutate(label = "Forest carbon (McMaster total vs SCANFI aboveground)") |> stats_table("kg C/m²") |> print()
  r <- mcm |> filter(a > 0, b > 0) |> summarise(q1 = quantile(a / b, 0.25), med = median(a / b), q3 = quantile(a / b, 0.75))
  cat(sprintf("\n\nWhere both are above zero, McMaster/WWF carbon is a median **%.2f×** SCANFI aboveground carbon (interquartile range %.2f–%.2f). A ratio above 1 is expected because McMaster includes belowground and dead pools; how far above 1, and where, is the part to check against pool ratios and against disagreement. Using the IPCC default carbon fraction of 0.47 instead of 0.5 would raise these ratios by about 6%%.\n",
              r$med, r$q1, r$q3))
}
```

### Aboveground biomass 2020 · SCANFI v1.2 vs ESA CCI v6

Both products map aboveground biomass for 2020 in Mg/ha. SCANFI (30 m) is averaged to the ESA CCI 100 m grid.

```{r}
agb <- read_pair_samples("agb")
if (!is.null(agb)) agb <- agb |> filter(a > 0 | b > 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: chart-agb-maps
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.3
#| fig-cap: !expr hex_caption(100000, 5)
if (!is.null(agb)) hex_trio(agb, "Mg/ha", "SCANFI v1.2", "ESA CCI v6")
```

```{r}
#| label: chart-agb
#| fig-height: 4.2
if (!is.null(agb)) {
  hex_pair(agb, "Mg/ha", "SCANFI", "ESA CCI", bins = 50) | ecozone_bias(agb, "Mg/ha", "SCANFI", "ESA CCI")
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(agb)) {
  agb |> group_by(id) |> agree_stats() |> mutate(label = "Aboveground biomass 2020") |> stats_table("Mg/ha") |> print()
  z <- agb |> summarise(only_a = mean(a > 0 & b == 0), only_b = mean(a == 0 & b > 0))
  cat(sprintf("\n\nOf the points where either product shows biomass, %s have biomass only in SCANFI and %s only in ESA CCI; these are differences in where forest is mapped rather than in how much biomass it holds.\n",
              percent(z$only_a, 0.1), percent(z$only_b, 0.1)))
}
```
